adjudication.rationale: Figure 1b visibly shows the actual model interface for pretraining: single-cell microscopy image input, structured caption input, tokenization, image encoder, Q-Former fusion, and masked image reconstruction. Figure 1c also shows downstream use of learned image embeddings from evaluation images, so the figure supports both pretraining and immediate evaluation routes.

selection_decisions.rationale: Figure 3 visibly shows a user natural-language biological question (“In this embryo brain slice, where would TP53 knockout have the strongest effect?”) entering OCellus and producing an output response, so it establishes the natural-language query-to-model interface for this route.

Figure 3 visibly shows a user natural-language biological question entering OCellus and a text response coming back. The right panel explicitly includes the prompt about a TP53 knockout effect in an embryo brain slice, so it grounds the natural-language query interface for OCellus-Agent rather than only an abstract architecture or benchmark summary.

adjudication.rationale: Figure 3 visibly shows the immediate user-facing interface for a natural-language biological query: a user asks, “In this embryo brain slice, where would TP53 knockout have the strongest effect?” and OCellus returns a textual answer. That directly supports the route from natural-language query to OCellus-Agent.
